confirmed.title: CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx and CvProjects.test.tsx fail intermittently: the first test does a cold dynamic import that hits the 5s timeout, and the late render then breaks later tests
confirmed.expected: Unit tests for the TODO-placeholder CTA and title rules pass every run.
confirmed.actual: 3 of 5 runs of `npx vitest run CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx CrumbifySheet.test.tsx CvSheet.test.tsx CvProjects.test.tsx Highlight.test.tsx` failed. In a further 3 runs, 2 failed. Every failure starts with the first test in a file giving 'Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.' (CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx:17, and also CvProjects.test.tsx:19). The later tests in the same file then fail with 'TestingLibraryElementError: Found multiple elements with the role "link" and name /Get it on the App Store/' (or /View on GitHub/). The imports that timed out resolve late and render into the next test's document.
confirmed.evidence: Each test calls vi.resetModules() in afterEach (CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx:13, CvProjects.test.tsx:15), then vi.doMock('@/content') followed by `await import('./CrumbifyCtas')` (lines 26/43/58/73/88; CvProjects lines 35/62/86). So the first import transforms the whole module graph cold inside the test body, and that counts against the default 5000ms testTimeout (vitest.config.ts sets none). Under parallel load (the reported vitest Duration was 20.56s, setup 34.37s) the cold import takes more than 5s. The timed-out test's render is not cleaned up before the next test, so the failures cascade. Runs: pass, pass, FAIL(3), FAIL(6), FAIL(2); then FAIL(6), pass, FAIL(4).
confirmed.suggestedFix: Do the first import outside the timed test body, or give these tests a longer timeout. For example, add a `beforeAll(async () => { await import('./CrumbifyCtas'); }, 30000)` warm-up (and the same in CvProjects.test.tsx), or pass a per-test timeout such as `it('...', async () => {...}, 20000)`. You can also set `testTimeout: 15000` in vitest.config.ts. Optionally, `await` the dynamic import before calling render and call `cleanup()` explicitly in afterEach, so a late render cannot leak into the next test.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced on the current HEAD. I ran `npx vitest run CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx CrumbifySheet.test.tsx CvSheet.test.tsx CvProjects.test.tsx Highlight.test.tsx` 8 times and 2 failed: run 5 of the first batch had 3 tests fail with 'Test timed out in 5000ms', and run 3 of the second batch failed as shown below. In that failing run, src/components/sheets/CvProjects.test.tsx:19 and :46 timed out at 5000ms. Then :70 failed with "TestingLibraryElementError: Found multiple elements with the role \"link\" and name /Video Automation Pipeline/", which is the cascade the reviewer described. Cause: vitest.config.ts sets no testTimeout, so the default 5000ms applies. Each test calls vi.resetModules() in afterEach (CvProjects.test.tsx:15, CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx:13) and then does `await import('./CvProjects')` / `await import('./CrumbifyCtas')` inside the timed test body (CvProjects :35/:62/:86; CrumbifyCtas :26/:43/:58/:73/:88). That cold module-graph transform can take more than 5s under load. When a test times out, its pending import still resolves later, and it renders into the next test's document after RTL's auto-cleanup has already run, so duplicate links appear. vitest.setup.ts only imports jest-dom and adds no extra cleanup. This is real, reproducible flakiness in the unit gate. It is not a product defect.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/sheets/CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx and src/components/sheets/CvProjects.test.tsx, give the dynamic-import tests enough time and keep the cascade from happening. (1) Add a longer timeout for these files: either call `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 20000 })` at the top of each describe block, or pass `20000` as the third argument of each `it(...)`. The alternative is `testTimeout: 15000` in the vitest.config.ts `test` block. (2) Import `cleanup` from '@testing-library/react' and call `cleanup()` as the first line of each afterEach, before `vi.resetModules()`. Optionally, also warm the module graph once with `beforeAll(async () => { await import('./CrumbifyCtas'); }, 30000)`, and the same for './CvProjects', so the first test does not pay the cold-transform cost inside its timeout. To verify, run the 5-file command 10 times in a row and confirm 0 failures.

confirmed.fix: In src/components/Tabs.tsx, add `aria-label={tab.label}` to the tab <button> (desktop and mobile variants share this element). confirmed.title: The vi.doMock + dynamic import() unit tests in CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx and CvProjects.test.tsx time out under parallel load, and the late render then breaks the next test
confirmed.expected: The unit test gate (npm test) is deterministic. Every test passes whenever the code is correct, whatever the machine load.
confirmed.actual: Each test calls vi.resetModules() and vi.doMock('@/content'), then runs `await import('./CrumbifyCtas')` (lines 26/43/58/73/88), or `await import('./CvProjects')` in CvProjects.test.tsx (lines 35/62/86). So every test transforms and evaluates the component's module graph again from cold, inside the default 5000ms test timeout. Under load, the first one or two tests in each file go over the limit with 'Error: Test timed out in 5000ms'. The timed-out test's async body keeps running and renders into the DOM after the next test has started. The next test then fails with 'TestingLibraryElementError: Found multiple elements with the role "link" and name /View on GitHub/' (or /Automated Publishing Platform/). This matches the intermittent CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx failure the fix writer reported. The same file pattern is also in VideoSheet.test.tsx.
confirmed.evidence: I started 3 `npx vitest run` processes at the same time from the repo root. Run 1: 2 failed, both in CvProjects.test.tsx ('renders the external project title as plain text...' timed out in 5000ms, then '...purple link...' found multiple elements with the role link). Run 2: 5 failed. In CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx, 'renders both CTAs...' and 'renders the GitHub CTA with no icon...' timed out in 5000ms, then 'hides only the App Store button...' found multiple elements with the role link and name /View on GitHub/. In CvProjects.test.tsx, 2 tests timed out. Run 3: all 143 passed. A single run with nothing else running passes all 143 tests.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Stop cold-importing inside each test. One option: mock '@/content' once with vi.mock plus a mutable fixture object (vi.hoisted) that each test changes before render, and import the component statically. The other option: pass the CTA data in as props or through a small pure helper and unit-test that. At the very least, import the component once in beforeAll and give these tests an explicit timeout, so a slow import cannot spill a late render into the next test.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced. CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx:26/43/58/73/88 each run vi.doMock('@/content') plus a cold `await import('./CrumbifyCtas')`, and afterEach calls vi.resetModules() (lines 12-15). CvProjects.test.tsx and VideoSheet.test.tsx use the same pattern. vitest.config.ts sets no testTimeout, so the 5000ms default applies. I ran two `npx vitest run` processes at the same time as a 160-test Playwright run. Run v1: 1 failed out of 143, 'CvProjects > renders the external project title as plain text, not a link, while its href is a TODO placeholder' with 'Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.' Run v2: all 143 passed. The unit gate is non-deterministic under load.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/sheets/CrumbifyCtas.test.tsx, CvProjects.test.tsx and VideoSheet.test.tsx, stop cold-importing inside each test. Use `const fixture = vi.hoisted(() => ({ crumbify: { ctas: [] as Cta[] } }))` with a top-level `vi.mock('@/content', () => fixture)`. Import the component statically at the top of the file. In each test, assign `fixture.crumbify.ctas = [...]` before render(). Remove vi.resetModules() and vi.doUnmock(). This works because the components read content at render time. If a component reads content at module load, move that read into the render body. As a minimum stop-gap, if any dynamic import remains, add `{ timeout: 20000 }` and call cleanup() in afterEach.

confirmed.title: The reduced-motion cross-fade e2e test is flaky: it reads opacity once after a fixed 50ms sleep, and gets 1 or 0 under load
confirmed.expected: The test proves that the incoming sheet passes through a partial opacity, and it does so reliably, whatever the machine load.
confirmed.actual: The test clicks the tab, runs page.waitForTimeout(50), and reads getComputedStyle(opacity) once. Whether that read lands inside the page's window (the 'in' stage switches at about 16ms and the fade ends at about 216ms) depends on scheduling. Under load the read sometimes comes back as 1 because it lands after the fade has finished. It also sometimes comes back as 0 because the 'in' stage has not been committed yet.
confirmed.evidence: I served out/ on :5105 and ran Playwright through a scratch config (fullyParallel, default workers). A full-suite `--repeat-each=5` run gave 1 failure out of 5 for this test: 'expect(received).toBeLessThan(1) Received: 1' at pile.spec.ts:509. `--repeat-each=20 -g "real cross-fade|hit-testable above|pile does not jump"` gave 5 failures out of 20 for this test: four 'Received: 1' at line 509 and one 'Received: 0' at line 508.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Measure inside the page instead of across the Playwright round trip. For example, before clicking, install a requestAnimationFrame sampler on #sheet-crumbify that records every computed opacity until transitionend, then assert that some recorded value is strictly between 0 and 1. Or listen for 'transitionrun' / 'transitionstart' with propertyName 'opacity' and check the running transition. A 0-to-1 fade then always yields an intermediate sample, whatever the load.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced. e2e/pile.spec.ts:502-509 does click, then waitForTimeout(50), then one getComputedStyle read, then asserts 0 < opacity < 1. With `--repeat-each=20 -g "real cross-fade|hit-testable above"` against out/ on :5205, with parallel vitest load, this test failed 7 of 20 times, each with 'expect(received).toBeLessThan(expected) Received: 1'. The single sample is taken after the page's roughly 216ms fade window has closed.
confirmed.fix: In e2e/pile.spec.ts around line 492, replace the waitForTimeout(50) single read with sampling inside the page. Before the click, run `await incoming.evaluate(el => { (window as any).__op = []; const tick = () => { (window as any).__op.push(Number(getComputedStyle(el).opacity)); if ((window as any).__op.length < 60) requestAnimationFrame(tick); }; requestAnimationFrame(tick); })`. Then click, then `await page.waitForFunction(() => (window as any).__op.length >= 60)`. Then assert that some sample v satisfies 0 < v < 1. Alternatively, assert that a 'transitionrun' event fires on #sheet-crumbify with propertyName 'opacity'.

confirmed.title: The mobile tab loop e2e test can count 0 tabs: toBeVisible() passes while the row is still aria-hidden before hydration
confirmed.expected: The test waits until the mobile tab buttons are exposed before counting them, so the `count > 0` check cannot fail on timing alone.
confirmed.actual: Tabs.tsx renders the mobile <nav> with aria-hidden and inert, at opacity 0, until usePile reaches phase 'done'. Before hydration the state is the SSR 'off' phase. Playwright's toBeVisible() treats opacity:0 as visible, so `await expect(nav).toBeVisible()` passes on the pre-hydration HTML. `nav.getByRole('button').count()` excludes aria-hidden elements, so it returns 0 if it runs before React has hydrated and applied the skip. This matches the reported intermittent failures of the 520/560/599px tab-width loop.
confirmed.evidence: `--repeat-each=20` on the same grep: 1 failure out of 20 in the 599px case (repeat14): 'expect(received).toBeGreaterThan(expected) Expected: > 0 Received: 0', which is the `expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0)` line right after the toBeVisible and count calls. The mechanism is in the source: Pile.tsx passes hidden={showIntro} to the mobile Tabs, and Tabs.tsx sets aria-hidden, inert and opacity 0 while hidden.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Wait for the tabs themselves, not the container. For example: `await expect(nav.getByRole('button')).toHaveCount(5)`, or `await expect(nav).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true')` before counting. The 390px layout test (line 58) and any other test that gates on the mobile nav's toBeVisible() should get the same change.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced, and the mechanism is confirmed. out/index.html ships `<nav ... data-variant="mobile" aria-hidden="true" inert="" style="opacity:0;pointer-events:none">` (Tabs.tsx:49-51, Pile.tsx:78 hidden={showIntro}). Playwright's toBeVisible() treats opacity:0 as visible, so e2e/pile.spec.ts:547 passes on the pre-hydration HTML. getByRole('button').count() excludes aria-hidden elements and returns 0. In my repeat-each=20 run, this test failed 3 times with 'Received: 0' at `expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0)`, once each at 560px, 430px and 520px.
confirmed.fix: In e2e/pile.spec.ts:547, replace `await expect(nav).toBeVisible()` with `await expect(nav).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true')`, followed by `await expect(nav.getByRole('button')).toHaveCount(5)`, before calling count(). Make the same change to any other test that gates on the mobile nav's toBeVisible(), such as the 390px layout test near line 58.

confirmed.title: The e2e check that the sticky note does not visually cover a mobile tab cannot fail any more, because the note now has pointer-events:none
confirmed.expected: The comment at e2e/pile.spec.ts:570-575 says what this check guards: 'what matters is which element actually wins the paint wherever the two boxes overlap... require the tab, not the note, to be on top there'. It should fail if the note is painted over a tab.
confirmed.actual: The round-6 fix for behaviour-03 added `pointer-events: none` to .note (StickyNote.module.css:28). document.elementFromPoint skips elements with pointer-events:none, so it always returns whatever is under the note. The check therefore passes even when the note fully covers every tab. The slice-rvat5-01 regression it was written to catch (the mobile tab row losing its `position:relative; z-index:1` in Tabs.module.css) would no longer be detected. The same blindness applies to the new GitHub-link tests (lines 605-628). They now only verify pointer-events and not visual coverage. The only other guard on the 540-660px nudge is a regex in StickyNote.test.tsx that checks the media query exists.
confirmed.evidence: I served out/ on :5105 at 560x844, /#cv. I injected CSS that removes the tab row's z-index and position and pulls the note over the tab row (top:-60px, left:0, width:500px, z-index:999). Screenshot scratchpad/review-r7/code-quality-security-tests/blind-560.png shows the yellow note completely hiding all 5 tabs. Running the test's exact overlap-centre elementFromPoint logic gave testCheckPasses=true for all 5 tabs. With the note's pointer-events briefly set back to auto, elementFromPoint at the same points returned the note for all 5 (actuallyOnTop='note').
confirmed.suggestedFix: In the visual-coverage parts of both loops, temporarily set the note's style.pointerEvents to 'auto' inside page.evaluate before calling elementFromPoint, and restore it afterwards. Alternatively, compare the computed stacking directly, for example by checking that elementsFromPoint(x, y) lists the tab before the note. Keep the existing pointer-events:none assertion as a separate check.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Reproduced. StickyNote.module.css:29 sets `pointer-events: none`, so document.elementFromPoint and elementsFromPoint both skip the note. I served out/ at 560x844, /#cv, and simulated the slice-rvat5-01 regression by setting the mobile nav to zIndex:auto and position:static. I also pulled the note to top:-60px. Screenshot blind3.png in my scratch dir shows the yellow note completely covering all 5 tabs. The test's exact elementFromPoint check still returned tabWins=true for all 5, and elementsFromPoint listed only BUTTON and NAV. The visual-coverage checks at e2e/pile.spec.ts:553-590 therefore cannot fail. The GitHub-link loop (lines ~600-628) is also blind to visual coverage, though it still correctly checks click pass-through.
confirmed.fix: In e2e/pile.spec.ts, the hit-test loop (~line 553) and the visual-coverage loop (~line 577) need a visual check the note cannot bypass. Inside the page.evaluate, set `note.style.pointerEvents = 'auto'` on the .note element, call elementFromPoint, and restore it to '' in a finally block. Then assert that the tab, not the note, is returned. Keep a separate assertion that getComputedStyle(note).pointerEvents === 'none' for the click-through guarantee. Apply the same temporary pointer-events toggle to the GitHub-link visual check if visual non-coverage is intended there.
